one_liner: Portable std::to_chars/from_chars reimplementation for pre-C++17 toolchains and MSVC, winning there and near-parity on GCC.
what_it_does: Boost.Charconv reimplements std::to_chars and std::from_chars (locale-independent, non-allocating, non-throwing) for integers base 2-36 and for float, double, long double, and __float128. The API mirrors the standard header exactly, same chars_format enum and from_chars_result/to_chars_result types, just under boost::charconv:: instead of std::, so it targets toolchains without full <charconv> support (down to C++11, GCC 5+, MSVC 2015+) rather than replacing a working stdlib implementation.
how_it_is_fast: to_chars for floats uses the Dragonbox shortest-round-trip algorithm (detail/dragonbox/dragonbox.hpp, floff.hpp for fixed format); from_chars for floats uses Daniel Lemire's fast_float parser (detail/fast_float/); 80-bit/128-bit long double and __float128 go through Ryu's generic 128-bit path (detail/ryu/ryu_generic_128.hpp); integer to_chars uses precomputed digit-count/significand lookup tables (integer_search_trees.hpp, significand_tables.hpp) for branch-light itoa. These are the same published algorithms most std::to_chars/from_chars implementations already use, so gains show up mainly where the target stdlib (MSVC's) hasn't adopted them as aggressively.
when_to_use: Targeting MSVC and needing float/double from_chars roughly 2-4x faster than std::from_chars (the largest measured win)
Building for a C++11/14 toolchain (GCC 5+, Clang 3.8+, MSVC 2015+) that lacks <charconv> entirely
Need to_chars/from_chars for __float128 or 80-bit long double, which std <charconv> doesn't cover
Already depend on Boost and want one to_chars/from_chars-shaped API across compilers instead of per-compiler fallbacks
High-volume uint32_t from_chars parsing on Linux/GCC, where Boost measures ~1.3x over std::from_chars
when_not_to_use: Already on a recent GCC/libstdc++ or Clang target, where most cells are near parity (0.97-1.0x) with std::to_chars/from_chars
Want a true header-only drop-in: charconv ships src/to_chars.cpp and src/from_chars.cpp as separately-compiled sources, plus Boost.Assert/Config/Core as dependencies
Parsing untrusted long double/__float128 strings over 1024 bytes, the one documented path where it allocates
Need an independent (non-maintainer) benchmark; the published numbers are run and maintained by the library's own authors
On Windows double/uint64_t to_chars, where Boost measured very slightly slower than std (15.26 vs 15.77; 2.06 vs 2.10)

integration.form: static lib | shared lib (compiled sources in src/; not header-only)
integration.dependencies: Boost.Assert, Boost.Config, Boost.Core; optional libquadmath for __float128/std::float128_t
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (GCC 5+, Clang 3.8+, MSVC 2015 / 19.24+, NVCC 12.8+ for optional CUDA); constexpr paths need C++14
integration.platforms: x86/x86_64/ARM on Linux, macOS, Windows; libquadmath path limited to Linux x86/x86_64/PPC64/IA64; partial CUDA and SYCL device support
integration.thread_safety: not documented explicitly; functions are stateless, non-allocating, non-throwing with no shared mutable state, so concurrent calls are safe like std::to_chars/from_chars
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — matches std::to_chars/from_chars signatures, enums, and result types exactly, but lives in boost::charconv:: rather than std::, so call sites must be renamed, not just #include-swapped

gotchas: Parsing a long double/__float128 string longer than 1024 bytes is the one documented path that allocates, despite the library's non-allocating claim elsewhere

The fixed-format float path (floff, Dragonbox-based) had buffer-overflow and internal-overflow bugs (issues #186, #190) fixed in 2024; a to_chars-with-precision correctness bug (#158) was also fixed; issue #166 (more to_chars problems) was still open as of the last check
__float128/std::float128_t support needs libquadmath and only builds on Linux x86/x86_64/PPC64/IA64
b2/CMake auto-detect and link libquadmath when available; other build systems must define BOOST_CHARCONV_HAS_QUADMATH and link it manually
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Boost.Charconv when you need an actual std::to_chars/from_chars-compatible surface (same enums, same result types) on a pre-C++17 toolchain, MSVC, or for __float128/long double, not a different API or output format. Pick c4core, rigtorp/CharConv, or jeaiii/itoa instead when you want larger, unambiguous wins on a modern GCC/Linux stack and don't need std-API compatibility.
verified_claims_summary: Maintainer-run benchmarks (test/STL_benchmark.cpp) on Linux GCC 13.1/libstdc++, Windows MSVC 14.3, and macOS ARM (M1 Pro) GCC 13.2 score Boost.Charconv against std::to_chars/from_chars, itself scored against std::printf/std::strtoX; results run from near-parity to ~1.3x in most cells, with the clearest wins on MSVC float/double from_chars (~2.0x/~4.2x) and Linux uint32_t from_chars (~1.3x), and a few Windows/ARM cells (double/uint64_t to_chars, ARM from_chars) slightly slower than std.
status_note: Actively maintained (last master commit 2026-08-13, CI/fuzzing/codecov all wired up); BSL-1.0 licensed and copyable, but as a Boost library it pulls in Boost.Assert/Config/Core and a compiled component rather than being a single vendorable header.
